message.content:
**Typical time‑difference**

| City | Standard time zone | Daylight‑saving time zone |
|------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| **Los Angeles** | Pacific Standard Time – UTC−08:00 | Pacific Daylight Time – UTC−07:00 |
| **Berlin**      | Central European Time – UTC+01:00 | Central European Summer Time – UTC+02:00 |

Because both regions change their clocks at roughly the same time each year, the gap stays essentially *constant* throughout most of the calendar year:

```
Berlin   : UTC+1 / UTC+2
Los Angeles : UTC–8 / UTC–7
Difference : 9 hours
```

So **Berlin is usually nine hours ahead of Los Angeles**.  
If it’s noon in Los Angeles, it will be 21:00 (9 p.m.) in Berlin.

---

### When the difference temporarily shifts

During the brief weeks around the clock‑change dates—when one side switches before the other—the offset can briefly become 8 or 10 hours instead of 9. For instance:

| Transition period | Difference |
|-------------------|------------|
| Early March (LA moves forward first) | 8 hours until Berlin follows |
| Late October/early November (Berlin moves back first) | 10 hours until Los Angeles follows |

These windows last only a few days, after which the normal 9‑hour spread resumes.

---

#### Quick check (current moment)

> If it's currently **12:30 PM PT**, add 9 hours → **09:30 AM CEST** in Berlin.

Feel free to let me know if you'd like the exact local time right now!
